takeaways: The "private equity home-buying ban" (Senate File 3173) passed the Minnesota Senate in spring 2026 but was stripped from the final housing bill in May, so it is not law. It would have stopped owners of more than 100 homes from buying more one- to four-unit homes.

Jason's numbers on investors: about 26,000 Twin Cities single-family homes (roughly 3.5%) are owned by investors with two or more properties, and the largest investors hold only about 16% of those. Most buyers lose homes to a cleaner offer, not to Wall Street.
The 2026 Minnesota tax bill, signed May 27, added a one-time boost of almost 15% to the Homestead Credit Refund. The income limit is just under $143,000, and you have to file Form M1PR to get it.
A separate Special Refund pays back part of a big jump in property tax (more than 12% and at least $100) with no income limit, up to about $1,000.

The Homestead Market Value Exclusion (since 2012) lowers the value you're taxed on. It's largest for lower-value homes and phases out completely around $517,000; on a typical $410,000 home it excludes about $9,600.
Homestead status doesn't transfer from the seller. New owners must apply with their county, or they can miss these programs for years.

The HOA Reform Act (HF 1268), signed in May 2026, mostly takes effect January 1, 2027: fines generally capped at $100 per violation, late-payment interest capped at 8%, late fees capped at $20 or 5%, three bids for contracts of $50,000 or more, no votes on contracts where a board member profits, 21 days' notice before rule changes, and protection from retaliation.

Under the same law, cities can no longer require an HOA for new communities created on or after January 1, 2027 (unless the developer asks), and HOAs can't ban parking a work vehicle in your own driveway.

faq.q: Did Minnesota ban private equity firms from buying homes?
faq.a: No. Senate File 3173 passed the Senate in 2026 but was removed from the final housing bill in May, so it did not become law. Jason expects similar bills to come back.

faq.q: How do I get the Minnesota Homestead Credit Refund?
faq.a: Own and live in your Minnesota home with homestead status, stay under the income limit (just under $143,000 for this round), and file Form M1PR with the Minnesota Department of Revenue. It isn't automatic.

faq.q: Does homestead status transfer when I buy a house?
faq.a: No. Homestead status doesn't carry over from the seller. Apply with your county after you buy; most counties let you do it online.

faq.q: How much can a Minnesota HOA fine me starting in 2027?
faq.a: Under HF 1268, most fines are capped at $100 per violation starting January 1, 2027, with exceptions for repeat violations, health and safety issues, property damage and using the home for business. The HOA must give you a written list of fines.

takeaways: A new arena for the Timberwolves and Lynx is being discussed to replace Target Center (opened 1990). The owners have said they'd fund it privately; City Center, the Warehouse District and the Farmers Market are the sites mentioned. As of the video, nothing was signed.

Boston Scientific is Maple Grove's largest employer, with roughly 4,000 workers there. It opened a 400,000-square-foot campus at Arbor Lakes and has more phases planned, which supports housing demand in Maple Grove, Plymouth and Brooklyn Park.

MSP Airport served 37.2 million passengers in 2024 and has a capital program of about $1.9 billion for 2026 to 2028. It supports around 93,000 jobs, which matters for Bloomington, Richfield and Eagan.
The I-494 rebuild through Edina, Richfield and Bloomington: phase one (about $377 million, with E-ZPass lanes) wraps up in fall 2026, and phase two runs 2027 to 2030 from I-35W toward Highway 77.
United Village is being built around Allianz Field in Saint Paul's Midway on the Green Line: restaurants and an office building are under construction, with a hotel targeted for 2027.
With about 28% of downtown Minneapolis office space empty, some towers are becoming apartments, including the Grain Exchange (232 apartments) near City Hall.

Meta is building an $800 million, 715,000-square-foot data center on 280 acres at UMore Park in Rosemount, a former World War II gunpowder plant. Its main local effect is property tax base rather than jobs.

faq.q: What is being built at UMore Park in Rosemount?
faq.a: A Meta data center: about 715,000 square feet on 280 acres, an $800 million project, on land that was a federal gunpowder plant in World War II and later owned by the University of Minnesota.

faq.q: When will the I-494 construction be finished?
faq.a: Phase one through Edina, Richfield and Bloomington was wrapping up in fall 2026, according to the video. Phase two, from I-35W toward Highway 77, is scheduled for 2027 to 2030.

faq.q: Is the Timberwolves' new arena approved?
faq.a: No. As of the video, the team's owners had said they'd pay for a new arena privately and might pick a site by the end of 2026, but nothing was signed and no site was chosen.

takeaways: Expo 2031 Minnesota USA is planned as an A1 International Horticultural Exposition, a world's fair about plants, food, water and energy, running May through October 2031 in Dakota County.
Organizers describe a 240-acre site with five climate biodomes, a USA Pavilion and pavilions from up to 80 countries, and project 4 to 6 million visitors.
The last world's fair in the United States was New Orleans in 1984.
After the fair, the plan is a "legacy district" with homes and amenities rather than clearing the site.
As of the video, no final site had been announced. Rosemount, Farmington and Hastings were the locations mentioned, because they still have large areas of open land.
Organizers say Expo 2031 is a nonprofit funded by federal and private sources, not local property taxes. Jason suggests watching how that plays out.

faq.a: A planned world's fair (an A1 International Horticultural Exposition) in Dakota County from May to October 2031, with pavilions from up to 80 countries and 4 to 6 million projected visitors.
In Dakota County. As of the video, the exact site hadn't been announced; Rosemount, Farmington and Hastings were the locations being discussed.

faq.q: Will Dakota County taxpayers pay for Expo 2031?
faq.a: Organizers say no: it's set up as a nonprofit funded by federal and private sources. Some county officials have said they want to make sure it stays that way.

takeaways: North Commons Park in North Minneapolis, built in 1907 on about 27 acres, is getting a $45 million rebuild, the park board's largest single investment, with a much larger field house planned to finish by 2027.

Chanhassen's new community center is planned at more than 180,000 square feet with two hockey rinks, a field house, a fitness center and a walking track; construction was scheduled to start in May 2026, with completion in 2028.
Saint Paul's Central Station project, about $130 million on the Green Line, plans a 20-story tower and a six-story building with about 300 apartments and ground-floor retail.

The Metro E Line, a 13-mile bus rapid transit route, connects Westgate Station in Saint Paul with Southdale in Edina along University, Hennepin and France Avenues; more than $1.3 billion of development has been built along it since 2014.
Blaine is building a $750 million, 70-acre town center next to the National Sports Center, with a hotel, food hall, a 3,000-seat stadium and housing.

Upper Harbor Terminal turns 48 acres of Mississippi riverfront in North Minneapolis into a $350 million district with about 520 homes, 20 acres of park and an 8,000-seat amphitheater targeted for the 2027 season.
Highland Bridge, on the former Ford plant site in Saint Paul, is a more than $1 billion neighborhood on 122 acres with about 3,800 homes and 55 acres of parks, built out over 10 to 15 years.

The $2.9 billion Green Line Extension adds 14.5 miles of light rail and 16 stations from downtown Minneapolis through St. Louis Park, Hopkins and Minnetonka to Eden Prairie, with opening planned for 2027.

faq.q: When does the Green Line Extension open?
faq.a: Opening was planned for 2027 as of the video, after testing. The line adds 14.5 miles and 16 stations between downtown Minneapolis and Eden Prairie, through St. Louis Park, Hopkins and Minnetonka.

faq.q: What is Highland Bridge in Saint Paul?
faq.a: A new neighborhood on the 122-acre former Ford plant site in Highland Park: about 3,800 homes, retail, offices and more than 55 acres of parks, built in phases over 10 to 15 years.

faq.q: Where does the Metro E Line run?
faq.a: About 13 miles from Westgate Station on the Green Line in Saint Paul to Southdale Transit Center in Edina, along University, Hennepin and France Avenues.

takeaways: Pick a suburb for how your daily life will work, not for its spot on a "best places" list. Each of these five is a great fit for the right buyer.

Maple Grove: newer homes, Arbor Lakes shopping and Elm Creek Park Reserve, but it's car-dependent. Downtown Minneapolis is about 20 to 25 minutes in light traffic and longer at rush hour on I-94 and I-494. Median sale price was in the mid-$400,000s in early 2026.

Eden Prairie: strong job base in the Golden Triangle, lakes and trails, with prices from the mid-$400,000s to mid-$500,000s. Budget for the full monthly cost: property taxes in the low 1% range and association fees on many townhomes.

Shakopee: more house for the money (typically low to mid-$400,000s), but downtown Minneapolis is about 24 miles away on Highway 169: about 30 minutes in light traffic and 45 to 50 at rush hour. Best for people who work nearby or remotely.

Brooklyn Park: larger homes in the low to mid-$300,000s close to Minneapolis, but many were built from the mid-1960s to early 1980s, so a thorough inspection of the roof, electrical, plumbing and windows matters.

Woodbury: newer, well-kept homes in the mid-$400,000s and strong retail, but it's east of Saint Paul. Downtown Minneapolis is about 30 minutes in light traffic and 45 or more at rush hour. The Gold Line bus rapid transit, opened in 2025, reaches downtown Saint Paul in about 30 minutes.

faq.q: Is Woodbury a good suburb if I work in Minneapolis?
faq.a: It can be a long drive: about 30 minutes in light traffic and 45 or more at rush hour, through Saint Paul on I-94. Woodbury fits best for people who work in Saint Paul or on the east side of the metro.

faq.q: What should I check when buying in Brooklyn Park?
faq.a: Many homes there were built from the mid-1960s to the early 1980s, so get a strong inspection and look closely at the electrical panel, roof, plumbing and windows, not just cosmetic updates.

faq.q: How long is the commute from Shakopee to downtown Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 30 minutes in light traffic on Highway 169, and often 45 to 50 minutes at rush hour, according to the video. Bus trips can take more than an hour.

takeaways: In most big U.S. cities, prices rise as you get closer to downtown. In the Twin Cities, many of the highest prices are in suburbs west of Minneapolis, such as Edina, Wayzata and Minnetonka and around Lake Minnetonka.
Downtown Minneapolis and Saint Paul condos can sit for months, while homes in suburbs such as Maple Grove, Plymouth and Eden Prairie often sell in about four to five weeks, close to asking price.
Many Twin Cities suburbs have their own downtowns and identities: Edina's 50th and France, Wayzata's lakefront downtown on Lake Minnetonka.
Minneapolis is built around winter, with an indoor skyway connecting about 80 downtown blocks. Buyers here value heated garages with floor drains, mudrooms, efficient windows and good insulation.

The Minneapolis Chain of Lakes (Bde Maka Ska, Lake Harriet, Lake of the Isles, Cedar Lake and Lake Nokomis) is public parkland with paths open to everyone year-round, and nearby neighborhoods like Linden Hills, Kenwood and East Isles are among the most competitive.
Lake Minnetonka covers more than 14,000 acres with more than 120 miles of shoreline.
Saint Paul has a more historic feel: Summit Avenue is known as the longest preserved stretch of Victorian-era homes in the country.

faq.q: Why are home prices higher in some Minneapolis suburbs than downtown?
faq.a: Many Twin Cities suburbs have their own downtowns, lakes and major employers, so demand is strongest in the suburban ring. Downtown condos can take months to sell, while suburban homes often sell in weeks.

faq.q: What home features matter for Minnesota winters?
faq.a: Heated garages with floor drains, mudrooms, energy-efficient windows, good insulation and newer heating systems. You can search for several of these in listings.
Yes. The Chain of Lakes, including Bde Maka Ska, Lake Harriet, Lake of the Isles and Cedar Lake, plus Lake Nokomis, is public parkland with paths open to everyone year-round.
